subject: maths
question: Pipe A can fill 50% of the tank in 6 hours and pipe B can completely fill the same tank in 18 hours. If both the pipes are opened at the same time, in how much time (in minutes) will the empty tank be completely filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by A to fill 100% = 6 × 2 = 12 hours, B = 18 hours.

Total work (LCM of 12, 18) = 36 units.

Combined Efficiency = (36 ÷ 12) + (36 ÷ 18) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hr.

Time taken = 36 ÷ 5 hours = (36 ÷ 5) × 60 minutes = 432 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 432 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A fills 50% of the tank in 6 hours ⇒ It fills 100% of the tank in 12 hours.

Pipe B completely fills the tank in 18 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 12
 36
 3
 
 

 B
 18
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 36 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Converting hours to minutes: Time = (36 ÷ 5) × 60

⇒ Time = 36 × 12 = 432 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 432 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Emptying Pipe (Leakage)

If an emptying pipe or leak is present, its efficiency is taken as negative. Net efficiency = (Filling Efficiency) − (Emptying Efficiency).

Fractional Work Method

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, the part of the tank filled by both in 1 hour is (1/x) + (1/y).

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by pipe A and pipe B is a : b, then the ratio of their efficiencies will be b : a.
